1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — adjust downward for the first 5–7 days.
2. Model underestimates prices during sustained upward trends — increase forecast slightly above recent 30-day average when trend is strong.
3. Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at +10% above immediate prior peak for 3–5 days.
4. Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals — add 1–2 days of mean reversion adjustment if price drops >5% from prior peak.
5. Model underestimates long-term (15+ day) price movements — increase forecast by 2–3% for horizon >15 days if recent 30-day average is rising.
6. Model overfits to short-term volatility — reduce forecast variance by 15–20% if 30-day moving average of residuals is high.
